papers.title: Molecular survey on vector-borne pathogens in urban and peri-urban rodents in Spain.
papers.abstract: Rodents are key reservoirs and spillover hosts of major pathogens at the wildlife-domestic-human interface, playing a pivotal role in the eco-epidemiology of vector-borne diseases. This study aimed to evaluate the circulation of Leishmania infantum, Bartonella spp., and Hepatozoon spp. in rodent populations from anthropized areas in Spain.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Researchers tested 345 urban rodents (rats and mice) across Spain and found that 8.1% carried disease-causing germs like Leishmania and Bartonella that can spread to humans.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: This shows that common city rodents can harbor and potentially spread serious diseases to pets and people, highlighting the need for better pest control and disease monitoring in urban areas.
aiSummary.limitations: The study only looked at samples from the spleen, so it might have missed infections in other parts of the body.

papers.title: Lyme disease as a rare trigger for autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
papers.abstract: Case report of Lyme disease triggering autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: This paper investigates aspects of tick-borne infections triggering autoimmune conditions.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Shows Lyme disease can rarely trigger serious blood disorders.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Molecular characterization of tick-borne piroplasms in captive megaherbivores in Thailand.
papers.abstract: Theileria and Babesia are emerging threats to wildlife health. This study investigated the presence and genetic identity of these parasites in large captive herbivores in Thailand.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Researchers tested blood from 31 large zoo animals in Thailand and found that over half (52%) were infected with tick-borne parasites. White rhinos had the highest infection rate at 75%.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: These parasites can threaten the health of endangered zoo animals and potentially spread to wild or domestic animals.
aiSummary.limitations: The study only looked at animals in Thai zoos.

papers.title: The repetitive genome of the Ixodes ricinus tick reveals transposable elements have driven genome evolution in ticks.
papers.abstract: High-quality genome assemblies of the Lyme disease tick vector Ixodes ricinus reveal that 69% of their DNA consists of transposable elements.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Scientists mapped the complete genetic code of Ixodes ricinus ticks and discovered that 69% of their DNA consists of 'jumping genes' - among the highest levels found in any animal.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Understanding tick genetics could help develop better ways to control these disease-carrying parasites.
aiSummary.limitations: More research is needed to understand how these genes affect tick biology and disease transmission.

papers.title: Seroprevalence of tick-borne pathogens in dogs from Costa Rica.
papers.abstract: Study of tick-borne pathogen prevalence in Costa Rican dogs including Babesia, Ehrlichia, and Anaplasma.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Research on tick-borne pathogen seroprevalence in dogs from Costa Rica.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Helps veterinarians understand disease risk in Central American dogs.
aiSummary.limitations: Regional study with limited geographic scope.

papers.title: Novel Borrelia species detected in ticks from wild birds.
papers.abstract: Investigation of Borrelia species diversity in ticks collected from wild birds, revealing potential novel strains.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Researchers found new Borrelia strains in ticks on wild birds that may represent novel species.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Wild birds may spread new types of Lyme-causing bacteria to new areas.
aiSummary.limitations: Further characterization needed to confirm species status.

papers.title: Climate change impacts on tick distribution in Northern Europe.
papers.abstract: Analysis of how changing climate is affecting the geographic range of disease-carrying ticks in Scandinavia.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Ticks carrying Lyme disease are expanding their range northward in Scandinavia as temperatures rise.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: More people in northern regions may be at risk for tick-borne diseases in coming years.
aiSummary.limitations: Projections depend on climate models which have inherent uncertainty.

papers.title: Bartonella henselae endocarditis in immunocompetent patients.
papers.abstract: Case series of culture-negative endocarditis caused by Bartonella henselae in patients without obvious immunodeficiency.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Several cases of heart valve infection caused by Bartonella from cat scratches, even in healthy adults.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Bartonella should be suspected in unexplained heart infections, especially in people with cat exposure.
aiSummary.limitations: Case series from a single center.

papers.title: Babesia microti prevalence in Ixodes scapularis across the northeastern United States.
papers.abstract: Large-scale survey of Babesia infection rates in deer ticks across endemic regions.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Up to 20% of deer ticks in some northeastern US areas carry Babesia parasites.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Babesiosis risk is higher than previously thought in many Lyme-endemic areas.
aiSummary.limitations: Infection rates vary significantly by location and year.

papers.title: Neurological manifestations of Lyme disease: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive review of neurological complications associated with Lyme borreliosis.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Review of how Lyme disease affects the nervous system, including facial palsy, meningitis, and neuropathy.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Helps doctors recognize and treat neurological Lyme disease appropriately.
aiSummary.limitations: Systematic review based on existing literature.

papers.title: Comparison of diagnostic tests for acute Lyme disease.
papers.abstract: Evaluation of serological and molecular methods for early Lyme disease diagnosis.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Standard two-tier antibody testing misses many early Lyme cases; newer tests show promise.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Better early diagnosis could lead to faster treatment and better outcomes.
aiSummary.limitations: No single test is perfect for early Lyme disease.

papers.title: Bartonella quintana infections in homeless populations.
papers.abstract: Epidemiological study of trench fever and related Bartonella infections among urban homeless.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: High rates of Bartonella quintana infection found in homeless populations, spread by body lice.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Highlights need for hygiene resources and medical screening for vulnerable populations.
aiSummary.limitations: Study focused on specific urban homeless communities.

papers.title: Treatment outcomes in severe babesiosis requiring exchange transfusion.
papers.abstract: Retrospective analysis of patients with severe Babesia infection treated with red blood cell exchange.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Exchange transfusion combined with antibiotics improved survival in severe babesiosis cases.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Provides evidence for aggressive treatment approach in life-threatening Babesia infections.
aiSummary.limitations: Retrospective study design.

papers.title: Tick bite prevention strategies: a comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: Evidence-based review of personal protective measures against tick bites.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Permethrin-treated clothing and DEET repellents are most effective at preventing tick bites.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Practical guidance for reducing tick-borne disease risk during outdoor activities.
aiSummary.limitations: Effectiveness varies by tick species and environmental conditions.

papers.title: Cat scratch disease presenting as granulomatous hepatitis.
papers.abstract: Case report of atypical Bartonella henselae infection affecting the liver.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Cat scratch disease can sometimes cause liver inflammation with granulomas.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Doctors should consider Bartonella in unexplained liver problems, especially with cat exposure.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Long-term outcomes after treatment for Lyme arthritis.
papers.abstract: Follow-up study of patients treated for Lyme arthritis examining joint outcomes over 5 years.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Most patients with Lyme arthritis recover fully after antibiotic treatment, though some have persistent joint symptoms.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Provides prognostic information for patients and doctors managing Lyme arthritis.
aiSummary.limitations: Some patients lost to follow-up over the study period.

papers.title: Congenital babesiosis: a case series and literature review.
papers.abstract: Review of mother-to-child transmission of Babesia infection during pregnancy.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Babesia can be transmitted from mother to baby during pregnancy, causing neonatal infections.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Pregnant women in endemic areas should be aware of babesiosis risk and prevention.
aiSummary.limitations: Congenital transmission is rare; limited case data available.

papers.title: Bartonella species in domestic cats: prevalence and zoonotic potential.
papers.abstract: Survey of Bartonella bacteremia in household cats and risk factors for human transmission.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: About 30% of healthy cats carry Bartonella bacteria in their blood, especially younger cats and strays.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Cat owners should practice flea control and avoid rough play that could lead to scratches.
aiSummary.limitations: Prevalence varies significantly by geographic region.

papers.title: Two-tier testing versus modified testing algorithms for Lyme disease diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Comparative analysis of different serological testing approaches for Lyme disease.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Modified testing algorithms using newer assays may improve early Lyme disease detection.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Updated testing approaches could help diagnose more patients sooner.
aiSummary.limitations: Different labs may have varying test performance.

papers.title: Persistent infection with Borrelia burgdorferi in mice after antibiotic treatment.
papers.abstract: Animal model study demonstrating bacterial persistence despite standard antibiotic therapy.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Lyme bacteria can survive antibiotic treatment in mouse tissues, remaining in a dormant state.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Helps explain why some patients may have persistent symptoms after standard treatment.
aiSummary.limitations: Mouse models may not fully represent human infection.

papers.title: Ocular bartonellosis: spectrum of disease and treatment outcomes.
papers.abstract: Review of eye manifestations of Bartonella infection including neuroretinitis.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Bartonella can cause various eye problems including optic nerve swelling with characteristic star pattern.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Eye doctors should consider Bartonella in unexplained vision loss, especially with cat exposure.
aiSummary.limitations: Many mild cases may go undiagnosed.

papers.title: Co-infection with multiple tick-borne pathogens in the northeastern United States.
papers.abstract: Study of simultaneous infection with Borrelia, Babesia, and Anaplasma from single tick bites.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Many patients bitten by ticks are infected with multiple pathogens simultaneously, complicating diagnosis.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Doctors should test for multiple tick-borne infections, especially when patients don't respond to initial treatment.
aiSummary.limitations: Study limited to specific endemic region.

papers.title: Emerging Babesia species in immunocompromised hosts.
papers.abstract: Case series and review of atypical Babesia infections in transplant and cancer patients.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Immunocompromised patients can develop severe, prolonged Babesia infections that are difficult to treat.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Transplant recipients and cancer patients in endemic areas need special monitoring for babesiosis.
aiSummary.limitations: Case-based review; prospective studies needed.

papers.title: Molecular detection of tick-borne pathogens in dogs from Nigeria.
papers.abstract: Survey of Ehrlichia, Babesia, and other tick-borne infections in Nigerian dogs.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Nearly 60% of tested dogs in Nigeria carried tick-borne pathogens like Ehrlichia and Babesia.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Shows tick-borne diseases are very common in Nigerian dogs, helping veterinarians know what to watch for.
aiSummary.limitations: Regional study from Nigeria only.

papers.title: Prevalence of Borrelia burgdorferi in Ixodes ricinus ticks in Bulgaria.
papers.abstract: Study of Lyme disease bacteria prevalence in ticks from Bulgarian urban parks.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 23-52% of ticks in Bulgarian parks carried Lyme disease bacteria, with highest rates in northern regions.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Identifies high-risk areas for Lyme disease in Bulgaria.
aiSummary.limitations: Only urban park areas surveyed.

papers.title: Isolated Optic Neuritis Revealing Lyme Disease in an Adolescent.
papers.abstract: Case of a 17-year-old with Lyme disease presenting as optic nerve inflammation.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: A teenager developed vision loss from Lyme disease affecting the optic nerve, recovering after 21 days of antibiotics.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Lyme disease can cause serious eye problems that might be mistaken for other conditions.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Early brain changes in Lyme disease are associated with clinical outcomes.
papers.abstract: fMRI study showing brain activity patterns predict recovery versus persistent symptoms in Lyme disease.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Patients who recovered from Lyme showed more brain activity early in illness compared to those who developed persistent symptoms.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Brain scans might help predict which patients will develop long-term problems.
aiSummary.limitations: Small study with only 20 Lyme patients.

papers.title: Optic disc edema associated with neuroborreliosis.
papers.abstract: Case of pediatric Lyme disease with optic nerve swelling treated with antibiotics and steroids.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: An 11-year-old with Lyme-related optic nerve swelling improved with antibiotics plus steroids.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Combined treatment may work better for Lyme-related eye complications.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Tick Infestation Among Stray Dogs of Urban Chișinău, Moldova.
papers.abstract: Survey of ticks and tick-borne pathogens on stray dogs in Moldova's capital.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Nearly half of stray dogs in Moldova had ticks, with 1 in 4 ticks carrying disease-causing pathogens.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Stray dogs with infected ticks in city parks pose health risks to people and pets.
aiSummary.limitations: Single city study over two years.

papers.title: Cutaneous Bacillary Angiomatosis: A Rare Infection in Immunocompromised Patients.
papers.abstract: Case of Bartonella-related skin lesions in a kidney transplant recipient.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: A transplant patient developed unusual skin growths caused by Bartonella infection, successfully treated with doxycycline.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Immunocompromised patients can develop unusual Bartonella manifestations requiring prolonged treatment.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case in transplant setting.

papers.title: Imaging glial activation in patients with post-treatment Lyme disease symptoms: a pilot study using [11C]DPA-713 PET.
papers.abstract: PET imaging study demonstrating brain inflammation in patients with persistent symptoms after Lyme disease treatment.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: PET scans showed elevated brain inflammation markers (TSPO) in all 12 PTLDS patients compared to 19 controls across 8 brain regions - first evidence of widespread neuroinflammation in PTLDS.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Provides physiological evidence that 'brain fog' in PTLDS has a biological basis, not psychosomatic. Suggests potential for immunotherapeutic approaches.
aiSummary.limitations: Small pilot study; larger studies needed to confirm findings.

papers.title: Association of small fiber neuropathy and post treatment Lyme disease syndrome.
papers.abstract: Study demonstrating objective nerve fiber damage in PTLDS patients using skin biopsy.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: All 10 PTLDS participants showed abnormal skin biopsies with reduced nerve fiber density. All had abnormal cerebral blood flow. 90% had abnormal epidermal nerve fiber density.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Small fiber neuropathy may serve as objective biomarker for PTLDS. Skin biopsy testing could improve diagnosis.
aiSummary.limitations: Small sample size of 10 participants.

papers.title: Dysautonomia following Lyme disease: a key component of post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome?
papers.abstract: Review examining the connection between Lyme disease, autonomic dysfunction, and POTS.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: PTLDS shares mechanisms with long COVID and ME/CFS. Non-length-dependent small fiber neuropathy suggests autonomic ganglia as target. Co-infections with Bartonella linked to POTS.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Provides framework for understanding POTS/dysautonomia in PTLDS patients. Suggests autonomic testing should be routine.
aiSummary.limitations: Review article synthesizing existing evidence.

papers.title: The Clinical, Symptom, and Quality-of-Life Characterization of a Well-Defined Group of Patients with Posttreatment Lyme Disease Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive characterization of 61 well-defined PTLDS patients from Johns Hopkins.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 61 well-characterized PTLDS patients showed severe fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, and cognitive problems significantly impacting quality of life.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Establishes rigorous case definition for PTLDS research. Biosamples available for future studies.
aiSummary.limitations: Single-center study from referral population.

papers.title: Risk of post-treatment Lyme disease in patients with ideally-treated early Lyme disease: A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Study showing 14% of optimally treated early Lyme patients develop PTLDS.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 14% of ideally-treated early Lyme disease patients developed PTLDS compared to 4% of controls - even perfect early treatment doesn't prevent all cases.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Demonstrates PTLDS is a real clinical entity occurring even with optimal treatment. Supports need for prevention research.
aiSummary.limitations: Single geographic region; requires replication.

papers.title: A comparison of genome-wide association analyses of persistent symptoms after Lyme disease, fibromyalgia, and ME/CFS.
papers.abstract: First large-scale genetic study of PTLDS identifying potential susceptibility loci.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 19.4% of treated Lyme patients met PTLDS criteria. Identified two suggestive genetic loci near IRX1 and GAS2. PTLDS genetics distinct from fibromyalgia and ME/CFS.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: First large-scale genetic study of PTLDS. May identify treatment targets and susceptibility markers.
aiSummary.limitations: Suggestive associations require replication in larger cohorts.

papers.title: A pilot study of disulfiram for individuals with persistent symptoms despite prior antibiotic treatment for Lyme disease.
papers.abstract: First clinical trial of disulfiram for PTLDS showing mixed results.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 6/9 participants showed clinically meaningful fatigue improvement. Lower doses better tolerated. High adverse event rate at higher doses led to early termination.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: First clinical trial of disulfiram for PTLDS. Suggests potential benefit but significant tolerability concerns.
aiSummary.limitations: Small pilot study terminated early due to adverse events.

papers.title: Disulfiram: Mechanisms, Applications, and Challenges.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive review of disulfiram mechanisms and side effects in Lyme treatment context.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Comprehensive review: disulfiram effective against Borrelia persisters in vitro. Multiple molecular targets. Significant side effect profile including neuropathy.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Provides mechanistic understanding for disulfiram use in Lyme. Highlights need for careful monitoring.
aiSummary.limitations: Review article; clinical evidence still limited.

papers.title: Neurobartonelloses: emerging from obscurity!
papers.abstract: Comprehensive review of neurological manifestations of Bartonella infections.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Comprehensive review of neurobartonellosis: neuroretinitis, encephalitis, peripheral neuropathies, and neuropsychiatric conditions. Multiple Bartonella species implicated.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Expands clinical awareness of neurobartonellosis. Should be considered in unexplained neurological presentations.
aiSummary.limitations: Review based on case reports and series; systematic data limited.

papers.title: Bartonella species bacteremia in association with adult psychosis.
papers.abstract: Study finding significant association between Bartonella bacteremia and psychotic symptoms in adults.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 43.2% of adults with psychosis had Bartonella DNA detected vs 14.3% of controls (p=0.021). Significant association between Bartonella bacteremia and psychotic symptoms.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Suggests Bartonella should be considered in workup of new-onset psychosis. Treatment may improve psychiatric outcomes.
aiSummary.limitations: Cross-sectional design cannot prove causation.

papers.title: Bartonella henselae bloodstream infection in a boy with pediatric acute-onset neuropsychiatric syndrome.
papers.abstract: Case report of PANS patient with documented Bartonella bacteremia responding to antimicrobial treatment.
papers.journal: Journal of Central Nervous System Disease

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 18-month psychosis in adolescent resolved with antimicrobial treatment for documented B. henselae bacteremia. Four hospitalizations before diagnosis.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Demonstrates dramatic psychiatric recovery possible with appropriate Bartonella treatment. Supports testing in PANS patients.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Crowd-sourced investigation of Bartonella-associated cutaneous lesions and neuropsychiatric symptoms.
papers.abstract: Large crowd-sourced study linking Bartonella skin lesions with neuropsychiatric symptoms.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Large crowd-sourced study linking Bartonella-associated skin lesions (striae-like) with neuropsychiatric symptoms including anxiety, depression, and cognitive dysfunction.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Skin findings may serve as clinical clue for Bartonella infection. Supports comprehensive workup in patients with unexplained psychiatric symptoms.
aiSummary.limitations: Self-reported data; requires clinical validation.

papers.title: Bartonella- and Borrelia-Related Disease Presenting as a Neurological Condition.
papers.abstract: Case demonstrating need for advanced molecular diagnostics in tick-borne infections.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Case report: spider bite led to myalgia, lymphadenopathy, hip dysfunction. Novel molecular testing confirmed Bartonella. Standard testing missed diagnosis.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Highlights limitations of standard serologic testing. Supports use of advanced molecular diagnostics (ddPCR, BAPGM enrichment).
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Blood Supplementation Enhances Bartonella henselae Growth and Molecular Detection of Bacterial DNA in Liquid Culture.
papers.abstract: Study demonstrating improved Bartonella detection with BAPGM enrichment culture.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: BAPGM enrichment culture significantly improves Bartonella detection. Triple draw approach captures additional positive cases missed by single blood draw.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Supports use of BAPGM enrichment for improved diagnostic sensitivity. Multiple blood draws recommended for optimal detection.
aiSummary.limitations: Specialized testing not widely available.

papers.title: Serial Testing Using BAPGM Platform May Enhance Sensitivity of Bartonella Detection in Bacteremic Human Patients.
papers.abstract: Study establishing evidence for triple blood draw testing protocol for Bartonella.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Triple blood draw over 1 week detected 33.3% positivity vs 12.7% with single draw (OR 3.4, p=0.02). Relapsing bacteremia pattern necessitates serial testing.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Establishes evidence base for triple draw testing protocol. Single negative test doesn't rule out infection.
aiSummary.limitations: Retrospective analysis; specialized testing required.

papers.title: Neurological and immunological dysfunction in two patients with Bartonella henselae bacteremia.
papers.abstract: Case reports of neurobartonellosis with immunological abnormalities.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Two cases of B. henselae bacteremia with neurological symptoms and immunological dysfunction. BAPGM enrichment culture detected infection missed by standard testing.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Neurobartonellosis should be considered in unexplained neurological symptoms with immunological abnormalities.
aiSummary.limitations: Two case reports only.

papers.title: Tafenoquine for Relapsing Babesiosis: A Case Series.
papers.abstract: Case series demonstrating tafenoquine efficacy in treatment-resistant babesiosis.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Multiple cases of relapsing babesiosis successfully treated with tafenoquine after failure of standard therapy.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Tafenoquine emerging as rescue therapy for treatment-resistant babesiosis. Important for immunocompromised patients.
aiSummary.limitations: Small case series; larger studies needed.

papers.title: Babesia microti Variant With Multiple Resistance Mutations in an Immunocompromised Patient.
papers.abstract: Case report of multi-drug resistant Babesia with documented resistance mutations.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Novel Y272S cytochrome b mutation plus additional resistance mutations in patient on atovaquone prophylaxis. Multiple resistance mechanisms can accumulate.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Prolonged atovaquone exposure can select for resistance. Combination therapy and close monitoring essential.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Broad Antimicrobial Resistance in Relapsing Babesiosis Successfully Treated With Tafenoquine.
papers.abstract: Case of dual resistance to standard Babesia therapies rescued with tafenoquine.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Patient developed resistance to both azithromycin (23S rRNA mutation) and atovaquone (cytb mutation). Tafenoquine successful as salvage therapy.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Dual resistance can develop during treatment. Tafenoquine provides option when standard agents fail.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Atovaquone-Proguanil: A Promising Therapy for Persistent Relapsing Babesiosis.
papers.abstract: Case of successful Malarone treatment for relapsing babesiosis in CLL patient.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: CLL patient with multiple relapses on standard therapy successfully treated with Malarone (atovaquone-proguanil) combination.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Atovaquone-proguanil may be more effective than atovaquone-azithromycin in some relapsing cases.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.

papers.title: Screening for Babesia microti in the U.S. Blood Supply.
papers.abstract: Landmark study establishing evidence base for blood donor Babesia screening.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Large-scale blood donor screening study. Antibody and PCR testing year-round in endemic states reduced transfusion-transmitted babesiosis risk.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Established evidence base for FDA blood donor screening recommendations. Identifies scope of asymptomatic infection.
aiSummary.limitations: Focused on endemic states only.

papers.title: Transfusion-transmitted Babesia spp.: epidemiology, regulation, and risk mitigation.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive review of transfusion-transmitted babesiosis and current regulatory landscape.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Comprehensive review of transfusion-transmitted babesiosis. FDA guidance requires testing in 14 endemic states. NAT screening significantly reduced but didn't eliminate cases.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Current regulatory framework and remaining gaps. Climate change expected to expand geographic risk.
aiSummary.limitations: Review article; some geographic areas have limited data.

papers.title: Preventing Transfusion-Transmitted Babesiosis.
papers.abstract: Review of TTB prevention strategies and blood safety measures.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: ~19% mortality in transfusion-transmitted babesiosis. Asymptomatic parasitemia can persist for months to years. Regional blood donor testing implemented since 2010.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: High mortality in TTB emphasizes importance of screening. Immunocompromised recipients at highest risk.
aiSummary.limitations: Review of existing literature.

papers.title: Evaluating polymicrobial immune responses in patients suffering from tick-borne diseases.
papers.abstract: Study showing majority of tick-borne disease patients have immune responses to multiple pathogens.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 65% of TBD patients showed immune response to multiple pathogens, not just Borrelia. 4-60% of Lyme patients co-infected with Babesia, Anaplasma, or Rickettsia.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Single pathogen testing may miss co-infections. Comprehensive tick-borne disease panels recommended.
aiSummary.limitations: Serological testing has inherent limitations.

papers.title: Complete Remission in Paralytic Late Tick-Borne Neurological Disease with Multiple Co-infections.
papers.abstract: Case series demonstrating recovery from severe co-infection-related paralysis with prolonged treatment.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 10 patients with severe paralytic tick-borne disease and multiple co-infections. 70% achieved complete remission with long-term combined antibiotic/antiparasitic treatment over ~20 months.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Demonstrates potential for recovery even in severe late-stage disease. Supports prolonged combination treatment for polymicrobial infections.
aiSummary.limitations: Small case series without controls.

papers.title: Human Babesia odocoilei and Bartonella spp. co-infections in the Americas.
papers.abstract: First documentation of B. odocoilei as human pathogen, commonly co-infected with Bartonella.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 6/7 chronically ill patients had Bartonella and B. odocoilei co-infection. First definitive DNA evidence of B. odocoilei in humans. Geographic distribution may be widespread.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: B. odocoilei not previously recognized as human pathogen. Co-infections more common than appreciated.
aiSummary.limitations: Small patient cohort.

papers.title: Coexistence of Borrelia spp. with different tick-borne pathogens in Ixodes ricinus ticks in Poland.
papers.abstract: Large tick survey demonstrating common co-infections in ticks biting humans.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 2,073 ticks analyzed. Multiple co-infections common. Pathogen interactions affect bacterial loads.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Co-infections common in ticks biting humans. Supports testing for multiple pathogens after tick bite.
aiSummary.limitations: Polish tick population may differ from other regions.

papers.title: Tick-Borne Co-Infections: Challenges in Molecular and Serologic Diagnoses.
papers.abstract: Review of diagnostic challenges for detecting multiple tick-borne pathogens.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: 19 tick-borne pathogens identified in US. Most transmitted by just two tick species. Standard diagnostic assays have significant limitations for detecting co-infections.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Improved multiplex diagnostics needed. Clinical suspicion should remain high even with negative single-pathogen tests.
aiSummary.limitations: Review focused on US tick-borne pathogens.

papers.title: Anorexia Nervosa Caused by Polymicrobial Tick-Borne Infections: A Case Study.
papers.abstract: Case of eating disorder resolving with antimicrobial treatment for tick-borne infections.

aiSummary.whatTheyFound: Adolescent female with anorexia nervosa found positive for Borrelia, Babesia, and Mycoplasma. Clinical presentation consistent with Bartonella. Symptoms resolved with antimicrobial treatment.
aiSummary.whyItMatters: Tick-borne infections may underlie some psychiatric diagnoses. Consider infectious etiology in treatment-resistant eating disorders.
aiSummary.limitations: Single case report.
